title: IMS Policy
purpose: A short, signed statement from top management of the organisation's commitments for quality, the environment and work health and safety, suited to its purpose and context, that gives a framework for its objectives.

questions.text: What does the organisation commit to for its customers and the quality of its work?
What environmental commitments apply (for example protecting the environment, preventing pollution, specific local matters)?
What work health and safety commitments apply (for example safe and healthy working conditions, eliminating hazards, consulting workers)?
Who signs the policy (name and position)?
How is the policy communicated and made available (induction, noticeboards, intranet, website)?

requiredSections: Purpose and scope of the policy
optionalSections: Commitment to meeting legal and other requirements
expectedRecords: Evidence the policy is communicated (induction records, noticeboard photo, intranet page)
Management review minutes showing the policy was reviewed
draftingRules: Keep it to about one page in plain language suitable for display.
Only commit to what the organisation can show it does; no claims it cannot evidence.
State commitments in the organisation's own words — do not quote or paraphrase standard text.
reviewerChecklist: Signed by the stated top-management role and dated
Every commitment matches what the organisation actually does
The scope matches the management-system scope statement
The communication method described is real and current

sources.title: Etcher ISO gap analysis workbook V2.0 — evidence examples (column G)

brandingInstructions: Use the organisation's confirmed legal or trading name in the header, its logo reference (describe where the logo goes — do not invent one) and its confirmed brand colours for headings and table header rows. Put the document-control block in the footer or on a cover table. If a branding value is not confirmed, leave a placeholder.
